Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.rationale: Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS", all express and implied warranties (merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, title, accuracy) are disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant that the technology is error-free, will meet Licensee's requirements, or that nonconformities to the Documentation will be corrected. A search of the Agreement shows no affirmative Licensor performance or conformance warranty anywhere; the only "warrants" language runs against Licensee or is mutual boilerplate about counsel. This is the walk-away position under the WARRANTY rule, so we insert an express warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformance of the Licensed Software to the Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, and carve it out of the disclaimer so the disclaimer does not swallow it. Fallback of 90 days/30 days is available.

If 12 months is not workable we can accept 90 days for the software and 30 days for services with the same remedies.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
input.rationale: Article VIX is a pure disclaimer: the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS", all express and implied warranties (merchantability, non-infringement, fitness, title, accuracy) are disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant that the technology is error-free, will meet Licensee's requirements, or that nonconformities to the Documentation will be corrected. A search of the Agreement shows no affirmative Licensor performance or conformance warranty anywhere; the only "warrants" language runs against Licensee or is mutual boilerplate about counsel. This is the walk-away position under the WARRANTY rule, so we insert an express warranty (workmanlike services, 12-month conformance of the Licensed Software to the Documentation, compliance with laws, no malicious code) with a repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, and carve it out of the disclaimer so the disclaimer does not swallow it. Fallback of 90 days/30 days is available.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

**Finding submitted: `missing` (medium severity, warranty).**

**What the document says.** Article VIX consists solely of a disclaimer. The Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS" without warranty of any kind; all express and implied warranties — merchantability, non-infringement, fitness for particular purpose, completeness, use, accuracy and title — are disclaimed; and Licensor affirmatively refuses to warrant that the technology is error-free, that it will meet Licensee's requirements, that operation will be uninterrupted or secure, or that nonconformities to the Documentation "CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED."

**Why it's a deviation.** A full-document search for "warrant" confirms there is no affirmative Licensor performance or conformance warranty anywhere — the only warranty language either runs against our client (p0049, p0129) or is mutual boilerplate about consulting counsel (p0159). Combined with the liability exclusion at p0130 (which expressly covers breach of express or implied warranty), our client has no contractual recourse if the platform fails to perform as documented. That is precisely the playbook walk-away position.

**The redline (validated ok:true).**
- **p0110** — narrow the disclaimer with a carve-out so it cannot swallow the new warranty: "EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH BELOW IN THIS ARTICLE VIX, THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN 'AS IS' BASIS…"
- **After p0116** — insert an express warranty: workmanlike performance of services, 12-month conformance of the Licensed Software to the Documentation (using the existing defined terms at p0006 and p0017), compliance with applicable laws, and no malicious code — with a repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy at Licensor's option.

The comment flags the 90-day/30-day fallback so the negotiation has somewhere to land if 12 months is resisted.

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

tools.description: Retrieve up to three approved clauses for the current rule. Use when memory is enabled and model language would improve consistency.

tools.description: Validate a proposed minimal redline before submitting a deviation or missing finding. Correct all returned errors and call again until ok:true.

tools.name: submit_finding
tools.description: Submit the final finding for this rule. After a successful call, stop calling tools.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXIII NON EXCLUSIVE REMEDY Termination of this Agreement by either party will be a nonexclusive remedy for breach and will be without prejudice to any other right or remedy of such party. NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or minimum-fee-on-termination is payable by Licensee (our client) anywhere in the Agreement, so the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs) is already met. The fee provisions (Art. V and the Monthly Notional Volume tiers, p0056-p0070) are purely usage-based per-trade fees plus a $2,500/month support fee (p0086); the only "in no event less than" floor in p0070 is (as drafted) directed at the Licensor and in any event is a true-up to actual recorded trade volume rather than a stipulated damages amount. Termination provisions (Art. IV p0049, Art. XXI p0138) impose no exit payment — Licensor merely retains the right to be paid for trades already performed — and Art. XXIII expressly bars termination damages against either party. Audit cost-shifting on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is an audit-cost allocation, not a Customer-payable penalty, and falls outside this rule. The rebate/share arrangements (p0075-p0076) run in our favour. No redline required.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.
Detection guidance:
Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXIII NON EXCLUSIVE REMEDY Termination of this Agreement by either party will be a nonexclusive remedy for breach and will be without prejudice to any other right or remedy of such party. NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND
input.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty, early-termination fee or minimum-fee-on-termination is payable by Licensee (our client) anywhere in the Agreement, so the preferred position (no Customer-payable LDs) is already met. The fee provisions (Art. V and the Monthly Notional Volume tiers, p0056-p0070) are purely usage-based per-trade fees plus a $2,500/month support fee (p0086); the only "in no event less than" floor in p0070 is (as drafted) directed at the Licensor and in any event is a true-up to actual recorded trade volume rather than a stipulated damages amount. Termination provisions (Art. IV p0049, Art. XXI p0138) impose no exit payment — Licensor merely retains the right to be paid for trades already performed — and Art. XXIII expressly bars termination damages against either party. Audit cost-shifting on a >5% discrepancy (p0064) is an audit-cost allocation, not a Customer-payable penalty, and falls outside this rule. The rebate/share arrangements (p0075-p0076) run in our favour. No redline required.

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: (b) The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly. In no event shall the amount payable by the Licensor be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded with the Licensed Technology multiplied by the applicable Fees set forth above.
input.rationale: The fee construct in Article V is purely usage-based: the US$7.50–US$5.00 per US$1 million tiers are volume discounts, and the highest band reached simply sets the blended rate (p0067). There is no committed floor, minimum notional volume, take-or-pay, or shortfall/penalty mechanic anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" return nothing relevant), and the only fixed charges are the $35,000 initial payment already advanced and the $2,500/month technical support fee for services actually provided — i.e., usage or ordered services only. The "in no event ... less than" language in p0070 is a floor keyed to trades actually recorded as executed on the platform, not a committed volume. The volume-based rebate in p0076 runs in our favour (Licensor pays us). This meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

I checked every place a Customer-payable stipulated amount could hide:

- **Fee/payment mechanics (Art. V, p0050–p0070 and the volume tiers):** purely usage-based per-US$1m trade fees, a $35,000 initial payment, and $2,500/month support (p0086). No minimum volume commitment and no shortfall charge. The one "in no event … less than" floor (p0070) is drafted against the *Licensor* and in substance is only a true-up to actual recorded trade volume — not a liquidated sum.
- **"Supplemental Payments" (p0074, p0078):** a 33% revenue share on amounts we actually *receive* from third parties, payable only within 10 days of receipt — contingent on collection, not a penalty.
- **Termination (Art. IV p0049, Art. XX–XXI p0134–p0138):** no early-termination fee, no acceleration of remaining term fees; Licensor only retains the right to be paid for trades already performed. Art. XXIII (p0142) affirmatively bars termination damages against either party.
- **Remedies/indemnity (Art. XI–XIII):** injunctive relief and indemnity, but no pre-agreed damages figure.
- **Audit costs (p0064):** shifting audit cost to us on a >5% discrepancy is an audit-cost allocation, not a liquidated damages or penalty payment, so it sits outside this rule (worth watching under an audit-rights rule if that threshold matters to you).

The rebate/bonus share arrangements (p0075–p0076) run in our favour, so nothing to flag there. Since the preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Licensee — is already satisfied, I made no edit.

**Finding: Missing — vendor insurance (severity: low)**

The agreement has no insurance clause at all. The only mention of "insurance" (p0051) simply allocates taxes, duties, insurance and shipping costs to our client — it imposes nothing on Licensor. Licensor supplies and supports the Licensed Technology through which we receive consolidated market data and transmit Spot FX orders, and it receives our output data for error reproduction (p0092) plus our Confidential Information, so it squarely fits the profile of a technology vendor that should carry standard coverages.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new General Provisions subsection (l), inserted after p0159 and before the execution block — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where Licensor touches our data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates of insurance on request, maintained through the term plus one year.

The covenant binds Licensor only, so it adds no obligation to our client. Fallback if pushed: E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline needed.

The fee architecture in Article V/§II–III is usage-based only:
- The **US$7.50 → US$5.00 per US$1 million tiers** are volume *discounts*, not commitments; the highest band reached in a month simply sets the blended rate for all trades that month (p0067).
- Fees are calculated on **actual Monthly Notional Volume** traded, with no committed floor (p0070 — the "in no event less than" language is keyed to trades actually recorded on the platform, not to a promised volume).
- The only fixed charges are the $35,000 initial payment (already advanced) and the $2,500/month technical support fee for services actually rendered — both "ordered services" under the playbook.
- Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "take or pay" and volume caps returned nothing relevant; the only volume-linked commitment is the 15% rebate in p0076, which runs **in our favour** (Licensor pays Licensee).

Note for the file (outside this rule's scope): the 36-month Initial Period with renewal solely "at the option of the Licensor" (p0049) and no Licensee termination-for-convenience right is a separate term/exit issue worth flagging under the termination rule — but it is not a purchase commitment, so it does not trigger MINCOMMIT.

input.summary: Insert Licensor transition-assistance, data-return and deletion-certification obligations into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor property on termination and is silent on our own data and on exit support, so we have added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our trade and account data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and then delete it and certify deletion. If six months is unworkable, we can accept 90 days of transition assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: (c) TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return or make available to Licensee, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all trade records, account records, reports and other data of or relating to Licensee that are stored in, generated through or otherwise held in connection with the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data"); and (iii) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and, upon Licensee's request, certify such deletion in writing to Licensee. Licensor shall not delete, withhold or condition access to Licensee Data prior to satisfying its obligations under this Section.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert Licensor transition-assistance, data-return and deletion-certification obligations into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor property on termination and is silent on our own data and on exit support, so we have added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our trade and account data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and then delete it and certify deletion. If six months is unworkable, we can accept 90 days of transition assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: (c) TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return or make available to Licensee, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all trade records, account records, reports and other data of or relating to Licensee that are stored in, generated through or otherwise held in connection with the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data"); and (iii) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and, upon Licensee's request, certify such deletion in writing to Licensee. Licensor shall not delete, withhold or condition access to Licensee Data prior to satisfying its obligations under this Section.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXI EFFECT OF TERMINATION Upon termination of this Agreement: for any reason (a) the rights and licenses granted to Licensee pursuant to this Agreement will automatically terminate, and (b) Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section. All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination of this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation on Licensor. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs one way only: licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensor materials back within five days and certify compliance, with all Licensor rights surviving. Searches for "return", "data", "transition" and "terminat" surface no export, retrieval, migration or deletion-certification duty for Licensor, and the confidentiality article (p0124) likewise binds only Licensee. Because this is a hosted FX trading platform where our trade and account records reside on Licensor's systems, silence leaves us exposed to loss of our own data on exit (the walk-away outcome). Inserted a new Article XXI(c) tracking the playbook preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return of Licensee Data within 30 days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; fallback of 90 days' assistance is flagged in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert Licensor transition-assistance, data-return and deletion-certification obligations into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor property on termination and is silent on our own data and on exit support, so we have added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our trade and account data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and then delete it and certify deletion. If six months is unworkable, we can accept 90 days of transition assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: (c) TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return or make available to Licensee, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all trade records, account records, reports and other data of or relating to Licensee that are stored in, generated through or otherwise held in connection with the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data"); and (iii) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and, upon Licensee's request, certify such deletion in writing to Licensee. Licensor shall not delete, withhold or condition access to Licensee Data prior to satisfying its obligations under this Section.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert Licensor transition-assistance, data-return and deletion-certification obligations into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor property on termination and is silent on our own data and on exit support, so we have added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our trade and account data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and then delete it and certify deletion. If six months is unworkable, we can accept 90 days of transition assistance with the same 30-day export.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation on Licensor. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs one way only: licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensor materials back within five days and certify compliance, with all Licensor rights surviving. Searches for "return", "data", "transition" and "terminat" surface no export, retrieval, migration or deletion-certification duty for Licensor, and the confidentiality article (p0124) likewise binds only Licensee. Because this is a hosted FX trading platform where our trade and account records reside on Licensor's systems, silence leaves us exposed to loss of our own data on exit (the walk-away outcome). Inserted a new Article XXI(c) tracking the playbook preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return of Licensee Data within 30 days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; fallback of 90 days' assistance is flagged in the comment.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee — our client); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert Licensor transition-assistance, data-return and deletion-certification obligations into Article XXI (Effect of Termination)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI only requires us to return Licensor property on termination and is silent on our own data and on exit support, so we have added a reciprocal obligation for Licensor to provide up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, return our trade and account data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and then delete it and certify deletion. If six months is unworkable, we can accept 90 days of transition assistance with the same 30-day export.

ops.text: (c) TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF LICENSEE DATA. Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return or make available to Licensee, in a commonly used, machine-readable format, all trade records, account records, reports and other data of or relating to Licensee that are stored in, generated through or otherwise held in connection with the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data"); and (iii) thereafter delete all Licensee Data from its systems and, upon Licensee's request, certify such deletion in writing to Licensee. Licensor shall not delete, withhold or condition access to Licensee Data prior to satisfying its obligations under this Section.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation on Licensor. Article XXI (Effect of Termination) runs one way only: licenses terminate immediately and Licensee must ship all Licensor materials back within five days and certify compliance, with all Licensor rights surviving. Searches for "return", "data", "transition" and "terminat" surface no export, retrieval, migration or deletion-certification duty for Licensor, and the confidentiality article (p0124) likewise binds only Licensee. Because this is a hosted FX trading platform where our trade and account records reside on Licensor's systems, silence leaves us exposed to loss of our own data on exit (the walk-away outcome). Inserted a new Article XXI(c) tracking the playbook preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return of Licensee Data within 30 days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; fallback of 90 days' assistance is flagged in the comment.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: TRANSITION — missing (medium), confidence 0.9**

- **What's in the document:** Article XXI (Effect of Termination, p0138) is entirely one-directional — our licenses cut off automatically, we must ship back all Licensed Technology, API documentation and Confidential Information within five days and certify compliance, and "all of the Licensor's rights ... shall survive."
- **What's absent:** No transition assistance, no data export/return, no deletion timing or certification running against Licensor. Text searches across the agreement ("terminat", "data", "return") and the confidentiality article confirm no such duty exists; the confidentiality obligations bind Licensee only.
- **Why it matters:** This is a hosted FX platform, so our trade and account records sit on Licensor's systems. Silence lands us at the playbook walk-away outcome (no data return / immediate deletion on termination).
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** New Article XXI(c) inserted after p0138 — six months' transition assistance at Licensor's then-current rates, machine-readable return of Licensee Data within 30 days, deletion plus written certification thereafter, and a bar on withholding or conditioning data access beforehand. The comment offers the 90-day fallback.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — FX Platform License Agreement (Customer-Side Review)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Licensor's draft License Agreement

## Executive summary

The draft is materially one-sided in the Licensor's favour and, as drafted, sits at or beyond our playbook walk-away thresholds in several places. The three critical items are risk allocation and ownership: there is no Licensor indemnity at all (Article XII runs only from us, and Article XIII(a) expressly excludes Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims); Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of fees paid, with no carve-outs, while our liability is unlimited; and Article III plus the "Derivative Work" definition give Licensor ownership of the bespoke front end and enhancements we commission and pay for under Article VII(b), with no provision confirming that our trading, order and client data remain ours.

A second cluster concerns control and exit. Licensor holds a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by seven years, with no non-renewal mechanism and no cap on fee increases, while we have no termination-for-convenience right at all. Licensor may terminate immediately on any Licensee breach with no materiality threshold or cure period, and Article XX(a) terminates our licenses on any Change of Control of Licensee unless Licensor consents — an effective veto over our own M&A. There is no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation on a hosted platform where our records sit on Licensor's systems, and no affirmative performance warranty (Article VIX is a pure "AS IS" disclaimer). Lower-priority gaps are audit procedure, a one-way three-year non-solicit, and the absence of any vendor insurance covenant.

Four rules are already compliant and require no redline: exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete and governing law (New York law with exclusive New York state and federal jurisdiction, no arbitration provision). One rule, MFN, could not be completed and needs manual review.

## Findings

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

XIII(a)–(b)) | Add a Licensor defence and indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with standard notice/control/cooperation, disapply the Article XIII limitations to it, and narrow our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of applicable law. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions (with Art. III, ¶0048; definitions ¶0005, ¶0008) | Insert customer-side carve-outs after ¶0048: assignment of custom deliverables we pay for (with licence-back of embedded Licensor IP), retention of all rights in our data, and no joint ownership. Licensor's pre-existing platform IP is preserved. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XIII) | Make the consequential-damages exclusion and the cap mutual, reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, add uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirm fee obligations are not damages for cap purposes. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions (with Art. XX(a)) | Add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Licensee, make consent mutual and subject to a reasonableness standard, bar Licensor assignment to our competitors, and delete the change-of-control termination/consent/re-pricing right. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II License Grant and Restrictions (Art. II(II)(c), (e); Art. IV) | Extend the grant to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (we remain responsible for compliance), confirm transferability to a successor, and limit termination to material breach uncured after 30 days' notice. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II License Grant and Restrictions (Arts. IV, XIX–XXI) | Add a Licensee right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Licensor has no mid-term convenience exit. | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § II License Grant and Restrictions | Grant is non-exclusive both ways; no sole-supplier or requirements covenant. No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation | No LDs, penalty or early-termination fee payable by us; Art. XXIII bars termination damages against either party. No redline. |

Binds the counterparty only. |

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as at or beyond our walk-away thresholds and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No Licensor indemnity plus a broad one-way Licensee indemnity**, compounded by the Article XIII(a) exclusion of Licensor liability for third-party IP infringement claims (INDEMN).
2. **Liability cap of one half of fees paid, benefiting Licensor only**, below the six-month floor, with unlimited Licensee liability and no carve-outs (LOL-CAP).
3. **Licensor's unilateral seven-year renewal option**, with no Licensee consent right and no cap on fee increases (RENEWAL).
4. **One-way non-solicit for the Term plus three years covering all Licensor and Affiliate personnel**, beyond the 24-month/all-personnel threshold (NOSOLICIT).
5. **Pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no affirmative performance warranty** (WARRANTY).
6. **Silence on transition assistance and data return** on a hosted platform holding our trade and account records (TRANSITION).
7. **Assignment and change-of-control provisions** — no affiliate/successor carve-out, no reasonableness standard, and Licensor consent effectively a veto over our own M&A under Article XX(a) (ASSIGN).

We would also treat the IP position (Licensor ownership of bespoke deliverables we pay for, and no confirmation that our data is ours) as a must-fix given its criticality.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline reflecting the proposals above, prioritising the three critical items (INDEMN, IP, LOL-CAP) and the exit cluster (RENEWAL, T4C, ASSIGN, TRANSITION) in the cover note.
2. Complete the manual MFN review before we send; we do not want to close on pricing terms with that rule unresolved.
3. Confirm with the business the operational inputs we need to hold the line: expected 12-month fee run-rate (to size the LOL-CAP figure), which Affiliates and contractors need platform access (LICENSE), and the realistic migration window off the platform (TRANSITION — six months preferred, 90 days as fallback).
4. Confirm with the deal team whether any near-term corporate transaction is contemplated, which would elevate ASSIGN and the Article XX(a) change-of-control trigger to a gating issue.
5. Note for the negotiation record that EXCLUSIVITY, LD, NONCOMPETE, GOVLAW and MINCOMMIT are already compliant, so we should resist any Licensor trade that reopens them.
